answer: Copying the same citations across 260 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 260 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the jetty index resolves every citation against the vine checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the nebula audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
